population.note: FICTIONAL ESTIMATES. About 57M of ~267M US adults are currently on an incretin (21.3%), for any indication. Age check: 0.20×12 + 0.33×20 + 0.24×32 + 0.23×20 = 2.4 + 6.6 + 7.68 + 4.6 ≈ 21.3. Income thirds (18/21/25) average to 21.3. The gap between bottom and top narrowed from 11 points to 7 because of $39–69 generic semaglutide and Medicaid obesity coverage in 31 states. Cycling arithmetic: ever 29% − current 21.3% = 7.7 pp of adults (~20.6M) have used and are off now. Restarting got cheaper, so about 38% of current users are restarters (0.38×21.3 ≈ 8.1 pp), and about 25% of those currently off had already cycled before (0.25×7.7 ≈ 1.9 pp). (8.1 + 1.9)/29 ≈ 34% of ever-users have stopped and restarted at least once. Payer mix of the 57M current users: Medicare ~14M (≈10.4M diabetes/CV/CKD/OSA-coded, 3.0M Continuity Model obesity-only, ~0.6M on the new mild-cognitive-impairment indication); Medicaid ~9.5M (≈4.5M diabetes-coded, 5.0M obesity-only in 31 states); commercial ~15M (≈8M coded, ≈6.5M employer obesity coverage, much of it generic-only, ~0.5M ACA marketplace); generic cash ~10M; brand cash/direct (Zepbound, Foundayo, retatrutide) ~4.5M; gray market ~4M. Sum: 14 + 9.5 + 15 + 10 + 4.5 + 4 = 57M. Public programmes pay for 23.5M, or 41%, the largest single payer. About 4M users (7%) have BMI <27 and no diabetes. They are 'metabolic health' and longevity users, almost all paying cash for generic semaglutide at low doses. Off-drug population: of the ~20.6M who stopped, roughly a third stopped for GI or other side effects, a quarter because of coverage or a lockout (fewer than in 2028 now that generics are cheap), and a growing share (~2M) after a DXA scan or a clinician's bone or muscle warning. Never-users who would qualify clinically are still the majority of adults with obesity. Most are lower-income men, rural residents and people in the 19 non-covering Medicaid states, the largest being Texas and Florida. Pediatric: ~1.1% of under-18s (~800k), mostly 12+, with generic semaglutide prescribed by pediatric obesity clinics. Roughly one child in three lives in a household where an adult is currently on the drug.

access.public_coverage: Medicare is now the largest single payer of incretin fills. Coded use (T2D, CV, CKD, OSA, MASH) sits in Part D as before. The CMS Medicare GLP-1 Continuity Model keeps its adherence conditions and its $245 ceiling, but under its existing payment terms Medicare pays the lesser of $245 or the product's net price. Generic semaglutide arrived in Jan 2030, and the model's fixed dollar budget now funds about twice the enrollment without any new rule. Enrollment is ~3.0M. Assume a blended net of ~60% generic at ~$55 and ~40% brand at $245, giving ≈$131/month. 3.0M × $131 × 12 ≈ $4.7B/yr, about the same dollars as 2028's $4.4B for double the people. Copay is $50 for brand and $10–15 for generic. The Feb 2030 tirzepatide indication for slowing cognitive decline in adults ≥60 with MCI and overweight/obesity is not a 'weight loss' use, so the statutory Part D exclusion does not apply. Plans began adding it mid-2030, and ~0.6M are on it so far. Medicaid: 31 states (up from 19) cover obesity, mostly with generic semaglutide at ~$45 net after rebates, for ~5.0M enrollees. 5.0M × $45 × 12 ≈ $2.7B gross, of which the federal share at ~65% FMAP ≈ $1.75B. That is less gross spending than 2028's $4.4B for more than three times the enrollees. The new states added coverage through ordinary P&T formulary decisions, not new law. Eleven states now attach adherence waivers.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India, Canada, Brazil, Mexico, Turkey and most of Southeast Asia have mature generic semaglutide markets at $8–40/month. Generic oral semaglutide is established in India. China has generic semaglutide and is the main source of unregulated tirzepatide and retatrutide API.
access.note: Price follows the generic-collapse path. A Sep 2029 patent settlement between Novo Nordisk and the Paragraph IV filers licensed generic semaglutide injection for US entry on 1 Jan 2030. Novo launched its own authorised generic the same day. By Q4 2030 six ANDA products plus the authorised generic sell at $39–69/month cash (Cost Plus-type pharmacies, Walmart, Kroger and Costco), the low end below $75. Tirzepatide and retatrutide remain brand-only until ~2031–32 or later. Lilly answered with Zepbound vials at $199–249 and Foundayo (oral) at $99–149 direct. Retatrutide fell from $399 to $349 direct cash, which is the top of the band. Wegovy's list price is unchanged and irrelevant. Employer coverage of weight management rose 44%→49% (Business Group on Health) because covering a $45 generic is cheaper than administering an exclusion. About half of the new coverage is 'generic semaglutide only, step-through required' before tirzepatide. New starts are now mostly injectable again, because the cheapest product is a pen; oral share of new starts fell from ~35% to ~25%. Gray market: demand left counterfeit semaglutide and moved to what is still expensive, 'research peptide' retatrutide and tirzepatide (~2M users). Personal importation shrank. Counterfeit and mislabelled pens imitating the new generics' unfamiliar packaging entered secondary wholesale and telehealth channels, and that became the public-health story of 2030. Total gray users are ~4M (7% of users, down from 13%), but the harms are larger and more visible.

on_market_classes: GLP-1 agonist, weekly injectable (semaglutide: Wegovy/Ozempic and, from Jan 2030, US generics and an authorised generic)
GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, Lilly; approved Feb 2028)
GLP-1 + amylin combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema; approved Dec 2026)
GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist, weekly injectable (survodutide, Boehringer Ingelheim; approved Jul 2030, MASH and obesity)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill, 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda and generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: smoking and nicotine-vaping cessation in adults with overweight or obesity (semaglutide, Sep 2028)
slowing of cognitive decline in adults ≥60 with mild cognitive impairment and overweight or obesity (tirzepatide, Feb 2030)
alcohol use disorder, reduction in heavy-drinking days (semaglutide, Sep 2030)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'metabolic health' and longevity dosing of generic semaglutide (0.25–1 mg weekly) in normal-weight adults, now mainstream in concierge and longevity clinics and in employer-adjacent telehealth (~4M users)
dementia prevention in cognitively normal older adults with a family history, off-label tirzepatide or generic semaglutide
nicotine cessation in normal-weight smokers and vapers
research-peptide retatrutide in gym and 'recomposition' communities
pediatric under-12 use under specialist care
drugs.pipeline_note: Approvals follow the envelope. Survodutide's phase 3 readouts were done and it filed Mar 2029. It was approved Jul 2030 (16 months later), with uptake led by MASH. Amycretin filed Jun 2029 and is under standard review, with a decision expected Q1 2031; it is not on the US market. MariTide (monthly) remains in phase 3 and has not filed. Bimagrumab and other muscle-preserving add-ons remain in phase 2 and are not on the market. The next_gen_launch driver (~30% triple agonist) is honoured by retatrutide, which was already approved. In 2029 its TRIUMPH extension data showed ~30% mean loss sustained at two years, Lilly expanded supply, and the cash price cut to $349 lifted users from ~0.6M to ~3M legitimate plus ~2M gray. The cognition_dementia driver is realised narrowly. Semaglutide's EVOKE trials failed in early Alzheimer's (2025), so Lilly's SURMOUNT-COG tested tirzepatide in adults ≥60 with MCI and overweight/obesity. It read out in May 2029 with ~22% slowing on CDR-SB at 18 months, a small absolute effect, and was approved Feb 2030 on priority review. The label does not claim dementia prevention. The semaglutide AUD phase 3 read out in 2029, and the indication was approved Sep 2030. Its label is the first incretin label to list apathy/anhedonia as an adverse reaction. Global incretin revenue is ~$118B (2030), roughly flat on far higher volume, with US semaglutide revenue collapsing into generics.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of side-effect discontinuation. Generic switching (new pen mechanics, different titration steps) produced a small 2030 bump in GI complaints and calls to poison control.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; Ozempic label 'not recommended in severe gastroparesis'; class labelling copied onto generics.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid loss; higher with retatrutide in real-world use.
No causal confirmation in long RCTs; absolute risk low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; MDL ongoing, first bellwether trials scheduled 2031.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Now recognised as a population-level problem. Medicare claims and DXA-cohort analyses (2029) show that users ≥65 who lose ≥15% of body weight lose on average 35–40% of it as lean mass, and that weight regained after stopping is disproportionately fat. Repeated cycling therefore ratchets body composition toward sarcopenic obesity. With ~34% of ever-users having cycled, geriatricians describe a cohort of 'thinner but weaker' older adults. Grip-strength and gait-speed declines appear in the Sentinel cycling study's interim report (2030).
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Nov 2029 FDA Drug Safety Communication and class labelling: assess muscle function at baseline in adults ≥65, counsel on resistance exercise and protein intake, and use caution with ≥20% loss in frail patients. Endocrine Society and AGS guidance favours slower titration and lower targets in older adults. No dose cap.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture in older and long-term users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: In a Sentinel/Medicare analysis (2029), women ≥65 who lost ≥15% had hip and vertebral fracture HR ~1.3 vs matched SGLT2 users, an absolute excess of roughly 2–3 fractures per 1,000 person-years. The excess concentrates in retatrutide users and in people with ≥3 years of continuous use. The findings confirmed the 2027–28 cohort abstracts. Men are affected less but measurably.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Included in the Nov 2029 class labelling: DXA at baseline for women ≥65 and men ≥70 and every two years on therapy, and consideration of bone-protective therapy. Medicare added DXA frequency coverage under existing benefit rules. No contraindication.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohorts still conflict; small absolute risk.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare' label for semaglutide; no US class label.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new evidence of causation, including in the AUD and smoking-cessation trials.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Warning removed from US labels (Jan 2026); not reinstated.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', apathy, anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: The semaglutide AUD phase 3 included the Snaith-Hamilton Pleasure Scale (SHAPS) as a psychiatric safety measure. Apathy/anhedonia adverse events were reported in 1.4% on drug vs 0.6% on placebo, an uncommon excess of under 1%, mostly at the top dose and mostly resolving after dose reduction. Subthreshold dulling is not captured. No obesity trial has measured it, so population prevalence among the 57M is still unknown.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed as an uncommon adverse reaction on the semaglutide AUD label (Sep 2030), not as a warning. Generic labels will carry it. Some addiction and psychiatry clinics now screen with SHAPS at 3 months. Obesity labels are not yet updated.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Roughly half of lost weight regained within a year off-drug. Coverage-driven stops have fallen with cheap generics, but Continuity lockouts and bone-related stops continue. Regain is now known to be fat-skewed (see lean mass).
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly; it underpins the adherence conditions.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: More reports at retatrutide-level intake reduction, including low protein intake contributing to the lean-mass problem.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Professional societies recommend baseline and annual labs; protein counselling now in class labelling.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years of continuous use; adolescents; repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: The 5-year cohort is growing fast; many 2025 Wegovy starters cross five years in 2030. The Sentinel cycling study's interim report links cycling to lean-mass ratcheting. Adolescent bone accrual is unstudied, and pediatric endocrinologists flag it as the next question.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Postmarketing requirements; Sentinel cycling study ongoing; FDA requested adolescent bone-density data from sponsors (2030).

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FDA adverse-event reports tied to non-approved product passed ~9,000 by late 2030. The Apr 2030 counterfeit-pen cluster had ~340 hospitalisations across 14 states, mostly hypoglycaemia and severe vomiting from pens labelled 0.25 mg that held 2.4 mg-equivalent, plus a Burkholderia-contaminated lot. Research-peptide retatrutide accounts for most tachycardia and endotoxin cases. Dose-unit confusion between generics with different concentrations is a separate, legal-product hazard.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Recalls and import alerts under existing authority; DSCSA serialisation enforcement against secondary wholesalers; FDA safety communication on generic pen concentrations. No new statute.

safety_ledger.effect: Acquired olfactory and taste dysfunction (hyposmia/dysgeusia) after ≥5 years of continuous GLP-1 RA use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A US claims replication (2029) found a weaker but consistent signal, HR ~1.3, absolute excess ~1–2 per 1,000 person-years after year 5. Confounding by diabetes duration is reduced but not excluded.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA PRAC concluded Mar 2029 and added 'hyposmia, frequency not known' to EU semaglutide and liraglutide labels. FDA still reviewing; no US label change.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Mostly mild and dose-related; more frequent in research-peptide users who skip titration.

food_and_beverage.state: GLP-1 households are ~33% of US households. Snack and confectionery unit volumes are down ~6–7% from 2026 and sugary drinks ~5%. The 'companion' protein lines that grew 2026–28 have commoditised, and the newer growth is in 'bone and muscle' SKUs (calcium-vitamin D-protein drinks, high-leucine snacks), marketed openly to older on-drug consumers after the FDA communication. A small premium counter-trend in full-fat, 'unmedicated appetite' artisanal foods (butcher-bakery chains in Brooklyn and Austin) grows fast from a tiny base. Midwest private-label snack plant consolidation continues.

alcohol.state: Spirits volumes are down a further ~4–5% over two years, and the Sep 2030 AUD approval makes heavy-drinker loss structural. Distillers lobby against payers covering semaglutide for AUD and lose. Beer is down ~2%. Non-alc keeps growing but small. Tobacco: US cigarette volume decline accelerates by roughly a point a year, and Altria cites generic semaglutide as a cessation competitor priced below a carton of cigarettes.

restaurants.state: Traffic is roughly flat and tickets are held up by small plates. Half-portion menus are standard. Buffets keep closing. In Manhattan, LA and Miami, high-end 'appetite' tasting rooms and steakhouses market abundance to an affluent off-drug or 'unmedicated' clientele and fill weekend books. Fast-casual protein bowls are still the volume winners.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep shrinking; Torrid and DXL closures continue. Mainstream retailers handle size churn from cyclers. Menswear and athleisure shift cuts toward 'built' fits (broader shoulders, thicker thighs) as muscle becomes the aspirational body. Women's activewear sells 'strong' rather than 'slim'.

fitness.state: Strength training is the growth story. Medicare Advantage plans expand fitness benefits to cover supervised resistance training for on-drug members after the bone and muscle labelling. DXA 'body comp' studios open in strip malls and charge $49–99 a scan. Big-box cardio gyms are flat-to-down. Gym communities are now the main distribution channel for research-peptide retatrutide.

insurance.state: Employer weight-management coverage is back up to 49%, mostly generic-only with step therapy, as pharmacy trend for the class falls sharply on generic semaglutide. Payers fight retatrutide cost through step edits. About 1 in 5 large self-funded employers keep BMI or adherence differentials, and several vendors add lean-mass or grip-strength metrics to biometric screening. Medicare and Medicaid absorb most older and poorer users.

pharma.state: Lilly dominates branded revenue with tirzepatide, retatrutide, Foundayo and the new MCI indication. Novo's US semaglutide revenue drops by more than half after the settlement; it bets on amycretin and CagriSema. Viatris, Teva, Sandoz, Dr. Reddy's and others split a fast-eroding generic market. Global incretin revenue is ~$118B, flat on much higher volume.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Thinness is cheap now and reads that way: 'generic thin' is the new sneer in affluent coastal circles, applied to a gaunt, low-muscle look associated with $49 pens and Medicaid. The scarce, prized body is muscular, dense and visibly fed: high lean-mass index on a DXA printout, thick forearms, an appetite on display. 'Unmedicated' is a boast in LA and Miami fitness and wellness culture, though many who say it take research-peptide retatrutide or low-dose generics quietly. Older thin women now face a new worry about the hip fracture rather than the dress size.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The price ladder has flattened, and the class marker has moved from thinness to body composition. Bottom-third on-drug rates rose to 18% on Medicaid and $39–69 generics. The affluent signal status with trainers, DXA scans, protein-heavy diets and either retatrutide's 'recomposition' at $349 or a carefully staged off-drug 'vitality'. In Ohio and Kentucky warehouse towns, the generic pen is an ordinary household item like blood pressure pills, with no prestige either way.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Half portions and protein-first remain normal in on-drug households. Among affluent 30–45-year-olds in Brooklyn, Silver Lake and Austin, eating a great deal in public (whole fish, steak for two, second desserts) has become a performance of health, of not needing the drug. Church potluck splits persist; 'Made Whole' congregations in Texas and Oklahoma now share stage space, uneasily, with secular appetite culture.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Profiles in New York and LA have moved from 'on it / off it' to 'unmedicated' and DXA-style lean-mass brags. Couples where one partner started the AUD or smoking indication describe calmer, sometimes flatter relationships; a minority now know the word anhedonia from the label. Mismatched appetites between on- and off-drug partners remain a common couples-therapy theme.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: The aesthetic inversion makes visible appetite a status good among the young affluent, just as medicine formally licenses the drug to quiet alcohol and nicotine wanting. Fat-liberation groups in Atlanta and Oakland find their language ('appetite is not a disease') borrowed by luxury restaurants and gym influencers they have little in common with. The meaning of appetite is now contested less by medicine than by marketing.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: Now acknowledged and bounded, but narrowly. The AUD phase 3 put the excess at ~0.8 percentage points of SHAPS-flagged apathy/anhedonia (1.4% vs 0.6%), mostly at the top dose and mostly reversible on dose reduction. That figure is now quoted everywhere as 'the' rate, though it comes from one population (heavy drinkers) and one scale, and misses milder dulling. Applied naively to 57M users it implies a few hundred thousand clinically flagged cases, a number nobody has verified.
interior_life.framing: Side effect, uncommon. Clinicians now say 'a small percentage of patients feel flat; lower the dose'. Most quieter wanting is still described as maturity, sobriety or discipline, and the label number lets the majority experience stay framed as character.
interior_life.effect_on_work: HR wellness vendors still cite fewer smoke breaks and steadier staff. A few sales organisations in Dallas and Atlanta quietly ask benefits consultants whether the AUD and cessation programmes they promote affect 'drive'; nobody puts it in writing. Employee assistance programmes add SHAPS screening to their AUD pathways because the label now mentions it.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Middle-aged bar leagues and late-night scenes keep thinning. The 'appetite' aesthetic gives young urban nightlife a maximalist edge: big dinners, loud rooms, sweat. A handful of musicians and comedians now joke openly about dose-lowering to 'get their edge back', and 'tapering for the tour' is a recognisable phrase in LA music circles.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Couples therapists cite the label to clients. The phrase 'it's on the label' gives partners permission to ask for a dose change, and some prescribers report requests to lower doses for libido or mood. Most couples still attribute contentment-without-passion to midlife.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The label number defuses the 'sedating the workforce' rhetoric: an uncommon side effect makes a weak conspiracy. Body-liberation and MAHA-aligned groups argue the number is an undercount because it came from one trial. No measurable change in participation.

state.regulatory_posture: No new state action this step: no new federal statute, mandate, coverage rule or surveillance regime. The FDA remains fast on approvals (tirzepatide MCI on priority review, survodutide, semaglutide AUD) and uses existing tools (DSCSA enforcement, recalls, import alerts, safety communications) against counterfeits without new authority. It remains understaffed for personal importation and research peptides. Public expansion happened through existing machinery: the patent settlement drove the price down, the Continuity Model's dollar-budgeted payment terms absorbed more enrollees, Medicaid P&T committees added coverage, and a non-weight indication sidestepped the Part D exclusion.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No mandate. Public programmes are de facto the default payer for older and low-income users (41% of users). This came from price and indication rather than legislation.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Unchanged in structure and wider in reach. The Continuity Model keeps its ≥80% PDC, ≥5% at 6 months and 12-month lockout, and now covers ~3M people. Eleven Medicaid states use matching adherence waivers. About 1 in 5 large self-funded employers keep BMI surcharges waived on biometric proof or connected-pen adherence. Some wellness vendors now also collect grip strength and DXA lean mass. Texas's ban on BMI surcharges in state-regulated plans stands, and ERISA plans remain exempt.
state.workforce_or_military: The Army and Air Force still issue accession waivers for recruits who reach standards on a GLP-1 with ≥6 months off-drug stability. Generic semaglutide makes pre-enlistment use near-universal among recruits who were overweight. Military physicians raise stress-fracture concerns in basic training for recent ex-users, and the Army begins a study.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Indian manufacturers (Dr. Reddy's, Sun, others) now supply the US legally through ANDAs, which closes much of the India–US price gap. China is the main source of unregulated tirzepatide and retatrutide API. Counterfeit generic-styled pens trace to repackagers routing through secondary wholesalers. Lilly and Novo still trade US concessions for tariff relief; generics are largely exempt from pharma tariffs.

events.event: Novo Nordisk settles patent litigation with generic filers, licensing US generic semaglutide injection from 1 January 2030 and launching its own authorised generic; by October 2030 seven products sell for $39–69 a month at major pharmacy chains.

FDA issues a Drug Safety Communication and class labelling on lean-mass and bone-density loss after Medicare data tie large losses in women over 65 to a 30% higher fracture risk; baseline DXA scans and resistance-exercise counselling are now recommended, with retatrutide users singled out.

FDA approves tirzepatide to slow cognitive decline in adults 60 and older with mild cognitive impairment and overweight or obesity, after a trial showing about 22% slowing at 18 months; because the use is not 'weight loss', Medicare Part D plans begin covering it mid-year.

Counterfeit 'generic semaglutide' pens sold through secondary wholesalers and two telehealth platforms put about 340 people in hospital across 14 states, from tenfold overdoses and a contaminated lot; FDA recalls product and warns that legitimate generics come in different concentrations.

KFF analysis finds Medicare and Medicaid now pay for 41% of incretin users, the largest single payer, as 31 Medicaid states cover obesity with generic semaglutide and Medicare's Continuity Model reaches 3 million enrollees on the same budget; no new legislation was involved.
FDA approves semaglutide for alcohol use disorder; the label is the first in the class to list apathy and anhedonia as an uncommon adverse reaction (1.4% vs 0.6% on placebo).

open_tensions: Medicare is now prescribing tirzepatide to people over 60 for cognitive decline while class labelling warns that the same people lose muscle and bone fastest. Nobody has studied whether the cognitive benefit outweighs a fracture excess of 2–3 per 1,000 person-years, and the cycling that Continuity lockouts force makes body composition worse.

Generic semaglutide made thinness a commodity, but tirzepatide and retatrutide stay brand until ~2031–32 or later. Unregulated demand has therefore moved to Chinese-sourced research peptides and counterfeit pens, and enforcement relies on tools Congress has not updated.

The anhedonia number (an excess under 1%, from one AUD trial) is now treated as settled for all 57M users, including normal-weight longevity users and adolescents who were never measured. A low official figure may now be blocking further study, much as the lack of any figure did before.

The new prized body (muscle, appetite, 'unmedicated vitality') is measured by DXA and grip strength, and wellness vendors have started collecting those metrics. Payer conditioning keyed to BMI is turning into conditioning keyed to body composition, with no law addressing either.
still_true: Wegovy's brand list price is still $1,349/month and almost nobody pays it.
The FDA's Jan 2026 removal of the suicidal-ideation warning from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels stands; it has not been reinstated.

The CMS Medicare GLP-1 Continuity Model's conditions are unchanged: ≥80% proportion-of-days-covered by refill data, ≥5% weight loss at 6 months, a 12-month re-enrollment lockout on lapse, and a $245/month payment ceiling.

Texas's 2027 law barring BMI-based premium surcharges in state-regulated plans stands, ERISA self-funded plans remain exempt, and about 1 in 5 large self-funded employers still attach BMI or adherence differentials.
The Army and Air Force accession waiver still requires recruits who reached standards on a GLP-1 to show ≥6 months of off-drug weight stability, and TRICARE covers obesity use only for active duty.

prose.headline: Thin Is Cheap Now: The $49 Pen, the Medicare Majority, and Why the Rich Want to Look Hungry
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2030 about 57 million American adults, a little over one in five, are on an incretin drug, and another 20 million have been on one and stopped. The figure rose less than the price fell. On New Year's Day generic semaglutide reached American pharmacies under a patent settlement Novo Nordisk signed rather than keep fighting a market it was losing anyway. By autumn seven versions sell for between $39 and $69 a month at Walmart, Costco and the online discount pharmacies. That is less than a carton of cigarettes, and Altria's filings say so.

Cheapness changed who pays. Nobody passed a law. Medicare's Continuity Model has always paid the lesser of $245 or a drug's net price, so when the net price fell to about $55 the same budget covered twice as many people. Thirty-one state Medicaid programmes now cover obesity, because covering a $45 generic costs less than the coverage the other states dropped. Then in February the FDA approved tirzepatide to slow cognitive decline in people over sixty with mild impairment. That is not a weight-loss use, so Medicare's old exclusion does not apply. Public programmes now pay for 41 percent of users, more than any employer or any wallet. For people who are older, poorer or both, the default prescription is a generic pen paid for by the government, with refill data watched for lapses.

The stronger drugs remain private. Lilly's retatrutide, now $349 a month, takes off nearly a third of body weight and has become the drug of the affluent and of gym culture. Gym culture also buys it from Chinese 'research peptide' sites at half the price. In April counterfeit pens dressed as the new generics put some 340 people in hospital across fourteen states. Some had pens holding ten times the labelled dose, and one lot was contaminated. The FDA recalled what it could find and warned that even the legitimate generics come in confusing strengths. It still lacks the staff to police the websites.

In November 2029 the drugs' largest physical cost became official. Medicare data showed that older women who lose a great deal of weight lose a large share of it as muscle, and break hips and vertebrae about 30 percent more often. Weight regained after stopping comes back mostly as fat. Labels now recommend bone scans and strength training. Medicare Advantage plans pay for resistance classes, and DXA scan studios have opened beside nail salons in strip malls. Geriatricians talk about patients who are thinner but weaker.

The culture has turned on itself. Once anyone can be thin for $49, thinness stops signalling anything, and among the affluent young in Brooklyn, Silver Lake and Miami the scarce body is dense, muscular and visibly fed. 'Generic thin' is an insult. 'Unmedicated' is a boast on dating profiles, sometimes true. Steakhouses market abundance. The fat-liberation organisers who coined 'appetite is not a disease' hear their slogan in luxury restaurant copy.

In September semaglutide was approved for alcohol use disorder, and its label became the first to list apathy and anhedonia, at 1.4 percent against 0.6 on placebo. The 'Ozempic personality' finally has a number, and the number is small. Clinicians say 'lower the dose', and couples therapists cite the label. Because the figure is official, few ask whether one trial in heavy drinkers says anything about four million normal-weight longevity users dosing for their metabolism.

The drug is now a utility, cheap, publicly paid for and monitored, and the trouble lies in its details: the bones of older users, the counterfeit pens, and a side-effect rate taken from one trial.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Denise Kowalczyk, 67, walks to the Kroger pharmacy in Toledo at nine because the refill is due today and the Continuity people count days. The pen is white now, not blue. The box says semaglutide, made in Hyderabad, copay $12. The tech reminds her it's the 1 milligram, not the 2.4 she had in March, and Denise says she knows, she knows.

At eleven she's at the hospital annex for the scan. She lies still while the arm passes over her hips. The printout says osteopenia, femoral neck. The nurse practitioner says the word 'fracture' gently and twice, and writes her a referral for the strength class Humana now pays for. Tuesdays and Thursdays, at the Y.

Her grandson Tyler picks her up. He is twenty-two and wide as a door, and he eats a breakfast burrito in the car and then half of hers. He says he's unmedicated. She saw the little vials in his gym bag at Easter and didn't ask.

At home she makes Ray's lunch, kielbasa and pierogi. She cooks it by memory more than by nose these days. The lilacs by the porch were faint this spring, and the doctor said it might be her age.

At three she does the band exercises off the printed sheet. Ten, rest, ten. Her arms shake.

At dinner Ray asks if she's happy. It's not a big question; he asks it about the pierogi too. She thinks about it and says she's fine. It's true. She's fine.

She sets the pen on the windowsill for Sunday.
